traits.stem_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: stems green; dark green, as Anderson's photograph shows them.

traits.spine_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: radial spines greyish, to 1 cm.

traits.central_spine_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: central spines greyish to blackish.

traits.areole_wool_colour.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) p. 14: the areoles' hairs red at first, turning black.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 649, Stenocereus thurberi: flowers funnelform, white, 4 to 8 cm long; fruit red. Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer pp. 22 to 25: flowers whitish to pinkish, 6 to 8 cm, with 25 or more perianth parts (as the family's default). Neither gives the flower's width or the fruit's size, so those stay set by hand.

traits.height_max_m.note: Britton and Rose vol. 2 (1920), as Lemaireocereus thurberi: usually trunkless, with 5 to 20 or more erect stems 3 m to 7 m tall.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Stenocereus thurberi (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.49 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.49, branches 0.49. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.flower_zone.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) p. 22, organ pipe cactus: showy sessile flowers, each from a single areole, near the apex and along the sides of the branches.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 2, 1920, p. 97), as Lemaireocereus thurberi: stems 15 to 20 cm thick, with 12 to 17 low, rounded ribs; areoles 1 to 1.5 cm apart, rarely 3 cm, large and brown-felted. The spines are not told apart as radials and centrals.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a clump of a dozen or more ribbed columns, 15 to 20 cm thick, that rise from a short base, spread out and curve up into a vase 3 to 7 m tall; new stems come from the base over decades. Pale flowers open near the stem tips, followed by red, spiny fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough stem heights from general knowledge: a few metres by 70 years, about 5 m by 120. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark green stems with 12 to 19 ribs, areoles 2 cm apart with dark felt, short dark radial spines and one to three longer centrals that grey with age; creamy white to lavender flowers. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): its tepals on a spiral (their count by hand: no flora counts them) on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, and a style with 5 to 15 stigma lobes, from the characters of Cactaceae and Stenocereus by the rules at the flowering plants. Its 200 stamens by hand, the most a flower draws, for the numerous ones every flora gives.
